$comment: The eleven decision kinds that have effect in M1 (build spec §3) and the two D2 adds for M2 (A.7: `qualification_approval`, `trust_activation`; SEAM.md §117), each with what its preview must bind. Derived from D1 A.8 with build spec §6 corrections 5 and 22, RN R4, and the per-kind table of Review B12 and B18. `subject_types` is what the decision is about; `options` the keys it can offer (a decision offers a subset where SEAM.md says so); `manifest` the keys its `dependency_manifest` holds at least, each a value that the approval must be unable to drift across; `effect` whether consuming it records an effect intent whose preconditions are checked again immediately before a journaled operation is made (D1 §10.5). Stop and Abandon act through the run-end protocol and record none. Tests read expectations from this file, never from the engine. The key names are the Verifier's (SEAM.md §76). `effect_options` names the options of a kind marked `effect: false` whose positive answer nevertheless records an effect intent: `finding_disposition`'s `alpha_exception` writes `findings.alpha_exception` as an effect (D2 §5 C1; SEAM.md §119). M3 slice 19 (D3 §3.3; T10; SEAM.md §218): the three `check_correction_*` manifests also bind `classifier_version`, `classifier_authority` and the proposal's `discovery`. The two trust kinds are engine-scoped: their decision rows have no project, and they are read and answered through `GET /v1/decisions` and `POST /v1/decisions/:d/answer` (SEAM.md §117). M4 slice 26 (D1 A.8; D4 §§2.4, 4.4, 4.6; E112; SEAM.md §275): `rollout_partial`, about a deploy operation whose attempt was reconciled `partial`, offering `retry`, `teardown` and `abandon`, its manifest binding the operation's status, the attempt, its deployment generation, the environment's current generation, the lease generation, the configuration identity, the adapter qualification, the reconciled read, the resource identities and the observations its effects were derived from; and `blocker`'s `teardown`, the preempting teardown a blocker of an ambiguous deploy offers (D4 §4.6). M4 slice 27 (D4 §6.3; J6; SEAM.md §293): `out_of_band_change` about an environment offers exactly `teardown` and `acknowledge` (no `adopt`), and its manifest also binds `resources` and `observation` (pinned by the cases, not here, so the repository kinds are unchanged). M5 slice 31 (D6 §3.4, §4.5, A.2, A.3; D1 A.8; SEAM.md §346): the products' decisions, each about the session `run` whose product it is: `idea_accept` (manifest: the baseline revision, the checkpoint's `blob`, the `idea_version` to record), `spec_approval` (the revision, the spec `blob`, its `semantic_digest`, the `spec_version` to allocate), `architecture_approval` and `plan_approval` (one `batch_key`; the `spec_version`, the `bundle` record, every proposed artifact's `blobs` by path, the `versions` publication will allocate, and for the plan its `plan_check` and `plan_generation`); and `spec_change` about a `spec_change_request` (the `spec_version`, the side ref's `proposal_revision`, the effective `protected_version`, the `impact` record and the impact's `dependency_manifest`), enabled by slice 31b's thin path (the driver's ruling; SEAM.md §§361, 371). Each offers `approve` and `reject`; `spec_approval`'s `approve` carries option blockers (D1 §9.7) where D6 §3.4 says. Targets: the four approvals 2 d, `spec_change` 3 d (D1 A.8). M5 slice 32 (D6 §8.1 steps 1 and 2; D1 A.8; K10; SEAM.md §§377, 379) adds `adoption_mode` (about the project; `full`, `scoped`; binding the pinned revision A, the signals and the policy) and `requirement_confirm` (about a requirement the retrofit session produced; `confirm`, `defect`, `withdraw`; binding the requirement's key, its exact text and criteria and the specification blob they were read from). M6 slice 40 (D7 §7.4, §10.3, §11, A.2; G5; objection 165; SEAM.md §§485, 486, 517) adds the design's three kinds: `design_approval` about a `design_revision` (`approve`, `revise`, `reject`, `approve_without_criteria`; binding §486's keys: the design version, the architecture version, the `design_check`, the asset manifest's version, the selection, the tree's blobs, the spec version it will be current against, the batched change's diff hash, the `inventory_digest`, the roadmap and plan versions; its effect is applied with the batched `spec_change`'s, so it records no intent of its own); `design_due` about the project (`open`, `waive`, `policy_off`, `later`; binding its `stage`, its `held_stages` and `stale_screens` (§517) and the policy revision; `policy_off` is a policy revision and records an intent); and `design_verdicts` about a `design_review` (`confirm`, `reject`; binding the review file's hash, `review_blob`, and its `evidence` records). Targets 2 d each. M6 slice 41 (D7 §4.5; E157 item 5; objection 170; SEAM.md §§491, 533): `finding_disposition` is also about a `design_finding` (a Designer's `contract_conflict` or `requirement_conflict`, routed to the owner, scope `design_conflict`), and its options include that question's `change_spec` and `architect`; `effect` stays `false` (`change_spec` makes a spec change request in the answer's transaction, `architect` records the route). S1 (E172 item 7; Sean's ruling of 2026-10-20; SEAM.md §555): `finding_disposition` of scope `reviewer_disagrees`, a Reviewer's disposition differing from the owner's, offers `keep`. No test reads a kind's `options` from this file; the list names the options a kind can offer as the sources state them, and is not complete for the owed scope (section 466), whose `fix` and `correct_check` M235 (g) pins. Rapid prototype to Alpha, slice E3 (the owner's ruling R5 of 2026-10-28; objection 218) adds `prototype_preparation_approval`, subject a `prototype_iteration`, options approve and reject, its manifest binding the role, provider, model, the run's token limit and its estimated cost and basis, whether it is paid, what it authorizes, the idea and the policy revision; no effect intent: its approve registers one `brief_preparation` work item in the answer's transaction. Rapid prototype to Alpha, slice E4 (Iterate; the owner's rulings R7 and R8 of 2026-10-28; objection 219): `prototype_preparation_approval`'s manifest also binds `continues` (null for a first iteration, else the predecessor and its brief) and `change` (null or the owner's change request).
